lv-2-chamber.q: This is step 1 of the 2-chamber. Which view is the line drawn on?
lv-2-chamber.alt: A long-axis view of the heart with a planning line through the mitral valve and the LV apex
lv-2-chamber.why: Step 1: on the 4-chamber, draw the line through the middle of the mitral valve and the LV apex.

lv-2-chamber.q: This is step 2, on the mid short axis. How should the line run?
lv-2-chamber.alt: Mid short-axis view with a planning line across the left ventricle
lv-2-chamber.right: Through the middle of the LV, parallel to the septum
wrong: Through the middle of the LV and the RV apex
Through the LVOT and the mitral valve
lv-2-chamber.why: Parallel to the septum gives the 2-chamber. A line through the RV apex gives the 4-chamber.

lv-2-chamber.q: Your 2-chamber shows the septum and part of the RV. What do you fix?
lv-2-chamber.right: Straighten the line on the mid short axis, so it's parallel to the septum
lv-2-chamber.why: With the line parallel to the septum, no septum or RV shows in the slice.

lv-2-chamber.q: The LV looks short on your 2-chamber. What's the likely cause?
lv-2-chamber.right: The plane is foreshortened: it misses the true apex
wrong: The field of view is too small
lv-2-chamber.why: A full-length LV has the true apex in the slice. Recheck the plane on the 4-chamber.

lv-4-chamber.q: This is step 1 of the 4-chamber, on the 2-chamber. What does the line go through?
lv-4-chamber.alt: Two-chamber view with a planning line along the left ventricle
lv-4-chamber.right: The middle of the mitral valve and the LV apex
wrong: The aortic valve and the LV apex
lv-4-chamber.why: Step 1: the line runs parallel to the long axis, through the middle of the mitral valve and the LV apex.

lv-4-chamber.q: On the mid short axis, the line goes through the middle of the LV. Where else should it reach?
lv-4-chamber.alt: Mid short-axis view with a planning line through the left ventricle, ending at a point marked in blue
lv-4-chamber.why: Step 4: fine-tune the line so it also reaches the RV apex, shown in blue.

lv-4-chamber.q: Why do you check the line on the basal short axis?
lv-4-chamber.right: To keep it clear of the LVOT
wrong: To center it on the aortic valve
To line it up with the papillary muscles
lv-4-chamber.why: Step 3: on the basal short axis, the line should stay clear of the LVOT.

lv-4-chamber.q: Your 4-chamber shows the LVOT and the aortic valve. What do you do?
lv-4-chamber.right: Replan from a mid short-axis slice: the plane is too far toward the base
wrong: Recheck it on the 2-chamber: the plane is foreshortened
lv-4-chamber.why: A good 4-chamber shows all four chambers with the mitral and tricuspid valves, and no LVOT or aortic valve.

lv-3-chamber.q: This is step 1 of the 3-chamber, on the basal short axis. What does the line go through?
lv-3-chamber.alt: Basal short-axis view with a planning line across it
lv-3-chamber.right: The middle of the LVOT and the mitral valve
wrong: The middle of the LV and the RV apex
lv-3-chamber.why: Step 1: on the basal short axis, draw the line through the middle of the LVOT and the mitral valve.

lv-3-chamber.q: What does a good 3-chamber show that a 2-chamber doesn't?
lv-3-chamber.right: The LVOT, the aortic valve and the aortic root
wrong: The tricuspid valve and the right atrium
lv-3-chamber.why: The 3-chamber has the mitral valve, aortic valve, LVOT and aortic root in one slice, with the LV and LA.

lv-3-chamber.q: The aortic valve looks narrow or clipped on your 3-chamber. What do you do?
lv-3-chamber.right: Replan the line on the basal short axis: it's off center
wrong: Recheck it on the 2-chamber: the plane is foreshortened
lv-3-chamber.why: The LVOT and aortic valve should be cut through the middle. Foreshortening is a different problem: it makes the LV look short.

lv-short-axis.q: How should the short-axis stack sit on the 2-chamber?
lv-short-axis.alt: Two-chamber view with a stack of parallel planning lines across the left ventricle
lv-short-axis.right: Perpendicular to the long axis of the LV, from the mitral valve plane to the apex
wrong: Parallel to the long axis, through the mitral valve and the apex
Straight across the chest, like an axial stack
lv-short-axis.why: Step 1: perpendicular to the long axis, from the mitral valve plane to the apex. Then check the same stack on the 4-chamber.

lv-short-axis.q: The base is cut off your stack. What happens to the volumes?
lv-short-axis.right: End-diastolic volume comes out too low
wrong: End-diastolic volume comes out too high
Nothing: the mid slices set the volumes
lv-short-axis.why: The stack has to cover the whole LV, from the mitral valve plane to the true apex. Add slices at the base.

lv-short-axis.q: What can a tilted stack do?
lv-short-axis.right: Make the walls look thicker than they are
wrong: Put dark bands across the heart
lv-short-axis.why: The slices should be perpendicular to the LV long axis on both the 2-chamber and the 4-chamber. Replan on both views.

lv-short-axis.q: Which slice thickness and gap does the guide give for the cines?
lv-short-axis.right: 6–8 mm, with or without a 2–4 mm gap
lv-short-axis.why: 6–8 mm, with or without a 2–4 mm gap, 10 mm in all. Thicker slices or larger gaps can miss small infarcts.

lv-short-axis-samples.q: Which basal slice is placed right?
lv-short-axis-samples.why: The right one has a full ring of myocardium, with no aortic root. The other is too close to the LVOT: move it toward the apex.

lv-short-axis-samples.q: Which level is this short-axis slice?
lv-short-axis-samples.alt: A short-axis cine slice of the left ventricle
lv-short-axis-samples.why: The papillary muscles are in the slice, which marks the mid level. The apex has a small cavity and no papillary muscles.

lv-short-axis-samples.q: Which describes a good apical slice?
lv-short-axis-samples.right: A small LV cavity, no papillary muscles, and no overlap with the mid slice
wrong: The aortic root and a moving valve in the slice
lv-short-axis-samples.why: The papillary muscles belong to the mid slice. A basal slice shouldn't show the aortic root either.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: Dark streaks cross this TrueFISP cine of the aortic valve. What's the artifact?
artifact-troubleshooting.alt: TrueFISP cine frame of the aortic valve with dark streaks across it
artifact-troubleshooting.why: TrueFISP loses signal in dark bands wherever the magnetic field is slightly off the center frequency.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: The guide lists the fixes for banding quickest first. Which comes first?
artifact-troubleshooting.right: Run a frequency scout and shift the center frequency
artifact-troubleshooting.why: Next come shimming over the heart only and a shorter TR. A GRE cine is the last step, if the band won't clear.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: What's the band of tissue that the arrow points to?
artifact-troubleshooting.alt: Axial image of the chest at the level of the great arteries, with an arrow pointing to a band of tissue across the top edge
artifact-troubleshooting.right: Wrap: the patient's back, folded over from outside the field of view
wrong: Breathing ghosts from the chest wall
Chemical shift (India ink) along the fat
artifact-troubleshooting.why: Anything outside the field of view in the phase-encode direction wraps onto the opposite edge. Here it doesn't reach the heart, so it could stay.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: The bright jet on this phase image has a black core. What do you do?
artifact-troubleshooting.alt: Phase image with a bright jet that has a black core
artifact-troubleshooting.why: It's velocity aliasing: anything faster than the VENC wraps to the opposite color. Use the lowest VENC that doesn't alias.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: One slice in a stack is smeared. Its neighbors are sharp, and so are the chest wall and liver. What's the likely cause?
artifact-troubleshooting.alt: A smeared cine slice with stacked arcs along the heart border, marked by an arrow
artifact-troubleshooting.right: Arrhythmia: each frame mixes heartbeats of different lengths
artifact-troubleshooting.why: The chest wall and liver stay sharp, so the breath-hold held. Repeat just the blurred slice first.

artifact-troubleshooting.q: The same LGE slice at two TIs, with the magnitude images on the left. Which row has the TI set right?
artifact-troubleshooting.alt: Four short-axis LGE images in two rows
artifact-troubleshooting.right: The bottom row: normal myocardium is black
wrong: The top row: the myocardium is gray
Either: the TI doesn't change a magnitude image
artifact-troubleshooting.why: On magnitude LGE, the right TI nulls normal myocardium, so scar stands out against it. The top row's TI is far too long.
